content: Richmond Medical Center is a large Kaiser Permanente hospital located in downtown Richmond, California. It provides healthcare services to approximately 77,000 members enrolled in its medical plans. The current facility was constructed in the 1970s to replace an older World War II-era field hospital. This field hospital originally served as the medical facility for the first Kaiser Hospital in Oakland. It was established in 1942 to cater to workers at the Richmond Kaiser Shipyards who were enrolled in the Kaiser Plan, one of the earliest voluntary pre-paid health plans, which later became a precursor to the modern Health Maintenance Organization (HMO). The field hospital ceased operations in 1995. Along with the surrounding Atchison Village neighborhood, the site is now listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is part of the Rosie the Riveter/World War II Home Front National Historical Park. Initially consisting of a single pavilion, the hospital expanded to three pavilions in the 1990s, upgrading to a full-service hospital with surgical and emergency services. As of 2006, the hospital is undergoing further expansion. Richmond Medical Center offers 41 departments and services to its members. Among these, emergency medical services are provided, including surgical care. Due to increased community demand, the emergency department is currently being expanded. The partial closure of the nearby Doctors Medical Center has placed additional strain on emergency services in the area. The hospital performs specialized surgeries, including bariatric surgery and head and neck surgery, in addition to standard surgical procedures. Patients with more complex medical conditions are now referred to John Muir Hospital in Walnut Creek, while pediatric patients requiring advanced care are directed to Oakland Children’s Hospital when medically safe or in life-threatening situations. In addition to emergency services, Kaiser Richmond provides a wide range of urgent care and routine medical services. The medical center specializes in various departments, including Benefits Advocacy and Social Services, which assist individuals enrolled in the state-funded Medi-Cal health plan. This program supports low-income individuals, seniors, and those with disabilities by helping them access their benefits and navigate applications and appeals. The center also offers Health Education workshops to promote healthy lifestyles and supports the Thrive/Viva Bien campaign. A Breast Health Clinic is available, focusing on preventative care and monitoring mammary health to reduce the risk of breast cancer. Additionally, the hospital has a dedicated HIV services unit to support HIV-positive patients. The Home Health Care and Chronic Conditions departments provide guidance for managing chronic illnesses such as dementia, asthma, diabetes, and epilepsy, as well as common conditions like seasonal allergies and influenza. These departments aim to help patients care for themselves or others at home without requiring frequent doctor visits. The Respiratory Care department focuses on asthma management, a condition prevalent in Richmond, often attributed to industrial pollution, particularly from the Chevron Refinery. The Rehabilitation department provides physical therapy for patients recovering from severe injuries or amputations. The Occupational Health department addresses work-related injuries and educates patients on prevention and treatment. A Speech Therapy department supports children with autism, while a Teen Clinic offers confidential appointments for adolescents, focusing on sexual health and substance use. This clinic collaborates with the Chemical Dependency department, which provides care for individuals dealing with addictions and substance abuse, including alcohol, marijuana, prescription drugs, and other narcotics. For toddlers, the Early Start unit offers motor skills and cognitive development programs, disease screening, and parental education on childcare. The hospital also features standard departments such as Allergy, Gastroenterology, Pathology, Pediatrics, Cardiology, Podiatry, Hospitalists, Psychiatry, Radiology, Dermatology, Internal Medicine, Dietetics, Outpatient Services, Neurology, Obstetrics/Gynecology, Ear, Nose & Throat, Oncology, Eye Clinic, and Orthopedics. The hospital is easily accessible via public transportation, with a shuttle service running every 15 minutes to the Richmond BART/Amtrak station, which is within walking distance. Several AC Transit bus lines are also nearby. Free parking is available for visitors in a six-story garage connected to the hospital by a covered walkway.
